title.raw: 卷20 文成五王 Volume 20: Emperor Wencheng's Five Princes

sentences.zh: 安樂王廣川王 齊郡王 河間王安豐王

translations.literal: Prince of Anle, Prince of Guangchuan, Prince of Qi commandery, Prince of Hejian, Prince of Anfeng
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Anle, Guangchuan, Qi commandery, Hejian, and Anfeng

sentences.zh: 安樂王長樂，皇興四年封建昌王，後改封安樂王。

translations.literal: Prince of Anle Changle, in the fourth year of Huangxing was enfeoffed Prince of Changchang, later changed to Prince of Anle.
translations.idiomatic: Changle, Prince of Anle, was made Prince of Changchang in Huangxing year 4 and later transferred to Anle.

sentences.zh: 長樂性凝重，顯祖器愛之。

translations.literal: Changle was by nature grave and steady; Xianzu valued and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Changle was sober and steady in temperament; Xianzu prized and favored him.

sentences.zh: 承明元年拜太尉，出為定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenming he was appointed Grand Commandant and sent out as Inspector of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenming year 1 he became Grand Commandant and went out as Dingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 鞭撻豪右，頓辱衣冠，多不奉法，為人所患。

translations.literal: He flogged powerful families and humiliated the gentry; many did not keep the law and were resented.
translations.idiomatic: He lashed powerful clans and shamed the gentry; many broke the law under him, and he was widely hated.

sentences.zh: 百姓詣闕訟其過。

translations.literal: The common people went to the capital to sue him for his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners went to the capital to accuse him of misconduct.

sentences.zh: 高祖罰杖三十。

translations.literal: Gaozu punished him with thirty strokes of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had him beaten thirty strokes with the staff.

sentences.zh: 貪暴彌甚，以罪徵詣京師。

translations.literal: His greed and violence grew worse; for crime he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His greed and brutality only deepened, until crimes brought him summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後與內行長乙肆虎謀為不軌，事發，賜死於家。

translations.literal: Later he and Inner-Steward Chief Yi Sihu plotted rebellion; when the affair broke out he was ordered to die at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he plotted treason with Inner-Steward Chief Yi Sihu; when it was exposed he was ordered to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 葬以王禮，諡曰厲。

translations.literal: He was buried with princely rites; posthumous title Li.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried with princely honors and given the posthumous name Li (Fierce).

sentences.zh: 子詮，字搜賢，襲。

translations.literal: His son Quan, style Souxian, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quan, styled Souxian, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，為涼州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was made Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shizong's reign he became Liangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 在州貪穢，政以賄成。

translations.literal: In the province he was greedy and corrupt; government was accomplished by bribes.
translations.idiomatic: In his province he was corrupt; office went to the highest bidder.

sentences.zh: 後除定州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was removed and made Inspector of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to the Dingzhou inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 及京兆王愉之反，詐言國變。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled, Yu falsely reported that the realm was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu of Jingzhao rose in rebellion, Yu spread false word of a dynastic crisis.

sentences.zh: 在北州鎮，咸疑朝廷有釁，遣使觀詮動靜。

translations.literal: The northern garrison provinces all suspected trouble at court and sent envoys to observe Quan's movements.
translations.idiomatic: Northern border provinces suspected trouble at court and sent agents to watch Quan.

sentences.zh: 詮具以狀告，州鎮帖然。

translations.literal: Quan reported the full situation; the provinces and garrisons were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Quan reported the facts in full, and the provinces and garrisons calmed.

sentences.zh: 愉奔信都，詮與李平、高殖等四面攻燒，[3]愉突門而出。

translations.literal: Yu fled to Xindu; Quan with Li Ping, Gao Zhi, and others attacked from four sides and set fires;[3] Yu burst through the gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yu fled to Xindu; Quan, Li Ping, Gao Zhi, and others besieged him from four sides and set fires;[3] Yu broke through the gate and escaped.

sentences.zh: 尋除侍中，兼以首告之功，除尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Palace Attendant; for merit in being first to report, he was also made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was palace attendant; for being first to report the rebellion he was also made left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰武康。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Wukang.

sentences.zh: 子鑒，字長文，襲。

translations.literal: His son Jian, style Changwen, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian, styled Changwen, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 後除相州刺史、北討大都督，討葛榮。

translations.literal: Later he was made Inspector of Xiang Province and Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign to attack Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Xiangzhou inspector and grand commander of the northern campaign against Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 仍兼尚書右僕射、北道行臺、尚書令，與都督裴衍共救信都。

translations.literal: He still held concurrent office as Right Vice Director, Northern Route Mobile Office, and Director of the Masters of Writing; with Commissioner Pei Yan he jointly relieved Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: He still held the right vice directorship, the northern route mobile office, and the directorship of the Masters of Writing, and with Commissioner Pei Yan relieved Xindu.

sentences.zh: 鑒既庸才，諸弟粗暴，見天下多事，遂謀反，降附葛榮。

translations.literal: Jian was a mediocrity; his younger brothers were violent and rough; seeing the realm in turmoil they plotted rebellion and surrendered to Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was a mediocrity and his brothers violent; when the realm fell into chaos they plotted rebellion and went over to Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 都督源子邕與裴衍合圍鑒，斬首傳洛，詔改其元氏。

translations.literal: Commissioner Yuan Ziyin with Pei Yan jointly besieged Jian; his head was sent to Luoyang; an edict changed their Yuan surname.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Yuan Ziyin and Pei Yan jointly besieged Jian; his head was sent to Luoyang, and an edict stripped the clan of the surname Yuan.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，許復本族，又特復鑒王爵，贈司空。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign restoration of the original clan was permitted; Jian's princely title was specially restored and he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Zhuang's accession the clan was allowed to resume its original name; Jian's princely title was specially restored and he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 鑒弟斌之，字子爽。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Binzhi, style Zishuang.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Binzhi, styled Zishuang.

sentences.zh: 性險無行，及與鑒反，敗，遂奔葛榮。

translations.literal: His nature was treacherous and without conduct; when he joined Jian in rebellion and was defeated, he fled to Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous and without principle, he joined Jian's rebellion; when it failed he fled to Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮滅，得還。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong was destroyed he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Rong's fall he was able to return.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，封潁川郡王，委以腹心之任。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Chu he was enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan commandery and entrusted with duties at the emperor's bosom.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Chu he was made Prince of Yingchuan commandery and given the emperor's innermost trust.

sentences.zh: 帝入關，斌之奔蕭衍，後還長安。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered the Pass, Binzhi fled to Xiao Yan; later he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered the Pass, Binzhi fled to Xiao Yan; he later returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 廣川王略，延興二年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangchuan Lue, in the second year of Yanxing was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Lue, Prince of Guangchuan, received his fief in Yanxing year 2.

sentences.zh: 位中都大官，性明敏，鞫獄稱平。

translations.literal: He held office as Grand Director of the Inner Palace; his nature was bright and keen, and in judging cases he was called fair.
translations.idiomatic: He served as grand director of the inner palace; bright and keen by nature, he won a name for fairness in trials.

sentences.zh: 太和四年薨，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he died; posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taihe year 4 and was posthumously titled Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子諧，字仲和，襲。

translations.literal: His son Xie, style Zhonghe, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xie, styled Zhonghe, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 十九年薨。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taihe year 19.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕宗室多故，從弟諧喪逝，悲痛摧割，不能已已。

translations.literal: An edict said: "My imperial clan has known many losses; my younger cousin Xie has passed away, and grief cuts me so I cannot stop.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "The imperial house has suffered too many losses; my cousin Xie is gone, and grief cuts so deep I cannot master it.

sentences.zh: 古者，大臣之喪，有三臨之禮，此蓋三公已上。

translations.literal: In antiquity, for the mourning of great ministers there was the rite of three personal visits—this applied to those of the rank of the Three Excellencies and above.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity great ministers were mourned with three personal visits—a rite reserved for the Three Excellencies and above.

sentences.zh: 至於卿司已下，故應。

translations.literal: As for ministers and offices below that, they should attend accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and offices below them were expected to attend in due measure.

sentences.zh: 闕自漢已降，多無此禮。

translations.literal: Since Han and downward the rite has largely been absent.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han times the rite has largely fallen away.

sentences.zh: 朕欲遵古典，哀感從情，雖以尊降伏，私痛寧爽。

translations.literal: I wish to follow the ancient canon and let compassion follow feeling; though I lower myself by rank, private pain will not be eased.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to follow the ancient canon and let compassion follow feeling; though rank demands restraint, private pain will not ease.

sentences.zh: 欲令諸王有期親者為之三臨，大功之親者為之再臨，小功緦麻為之一臨。

translations.literal: I wish princes with kin in the period of mourning to make three visits, those of great-achievement kin to make two visits, and those of lesser-achievement and finest-mourning kin to make one visit.
translations.idiomatic: I would have princes in the closest mourning circle pay three visits, those in the great-achievement circle two, and those in lesser or finest mourning one.

sentences.zh: 廣川王於朕大功，必欲再臨。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangchuan bears to me a great-achievement bond; I must certainly pay two visits.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guangchuan stands to me in the great-achievement circle; I shall certainly mourn him twice.

sentences.zh: 再臨者，欲於大殮之日，親臨盡哀，成服之後，緦衰而弔。

translations.literal: The two visits mean: on the day of the great encoffment, to come in person and exhaust grief; after the mourning garments are complete, to go in finest hemp and offer condolence.
translations.idiomatic: By two visits I mean: on the day of the great encoffment to come in person and exhaust grief, and after the mourning garments are complete to return in finest hemp and offer condolence.

sentences.zh: 既殯之緦麻，理在無疑，大殮之臨，當否如何？

translations.literal: For finest-mourning kin after the encoffment there is no doubt in principle; as for the visit at the great encoffment—is it fitting or not?
translations.idiomatic: Condolence in finest hemp after encoffment is plainly required; but is a visit at the great encoffment itself fitting?

sentences.zh: 為須撫柩於始喪，為應盡哀於闔棺？

translations.literal: Must one comfort the bier at the first mourning, or should one exhaust grief at the closing of the coffin?
translations.idiomatic: Should one comfort the bier at the first mourning, or exhaust grief only when the coffin is closed?

sentences.zh: 早晚之宜，擇其厥中。

translations.literal: As to whether early or late is proper, choose the mean between them.
translations.idiomatic: Whether early or late is better—choose the mean."

sentences.zh: 」黃門侍郎崔光、宋弁，通直常侍劉芳，典命下大夫李元凱，中書侍郎高聰等議曰：[4]「三臨之事，乃自古禮，爰及漢魏，行之者稀。

translations.literal: " Yellow Gate Attendant Cui Guang, Song Bian, Regular Attendant of Direct Transmission Liu Fang, Master of Ceremonies Lower Grandee Li Yuankai, Secretariat Attendant Gao Cong, and others deliberated:[4] "The matter of three visits is indeed an ancient rite; even through Han and Wei it has rarely been practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang and Song Bian of the Yellow Gate, Liu Fang, regular attendant of direct transmission, Li Yuankai, master of ceremonies lower grandee, Gao Cong, secretariat attendant, and others replied:[4] "Three visits are an ancient rite, yet from Han through Wei few have practiced it.

sentences.zh: 陛下至聖慈仁，方遵前軌，志必哀喪，慮同寧戚。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is supremely sagely and benevolent and is about to follow the former track; your will must mourn the dead and your thought is the same as dwelling in the mourning hut.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is supremely sagely and benevolent and means to follow the former track; your will is true mourning, your heart the same as one dwelling in the mourning hut.

sentences.zh: 臣等以為若期親三臨，大功宜再。

translations.literal: We your subjects consider that if period kin make three visits, great-achievement kin should make two.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that if the closest kin pay three visits, great-achievement kin should pay two.

sentences.zh: 始喪之初，哀之至極，既以情降，宜從始喪。

translations.literal: At the beginning of first mourning grief is at its utmost; since feeling has already lowered rank, one should follow the beginning of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of mourning grief is at its height; since feeling has already bent rank, the first visit should fall at the beginning of mourning.

sentences.zh: 大殮之臨，伏如聖旨。

translations.literal: As for the visit at the great encoffment, we bow to the sagely edict.
translations.idiomatic: As for the visit at the great encoffment, we bow to Your Majesty's intent."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「魏晉已來，親臨多闕，至於戚臣，必於東堂哭之。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Since Wei and Jin, personal visits have largely been wanting; for kin among ministers one necessarily wept in the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Since Wei and Jin, emperors have rarely mourned in person; for ministerial kin they wept in the Eastern Hall instead.

sentences.zh: 頃大司馬、安定王薨，朕既臨之後，復更受慰於東堂，今日之事，應更哭否？

translations.literal: Recently when Grand Marshal, Prince of Anding, died, after I had already visited him I again received condolences in the Eastern Hall; for today's affair, should I weep again?
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Marshal, Prince of Anding, died I visited him in person and still received condolences in the Eastern Hall; for today's rite, should I weep there again?"

sentences.zh: 」光等議曰：「東堂之哭，蓋以不臨之故。

translations.literal: Guang and the others deliberated: "Weeping in the Eastern Hall was because one did not visit in person.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and the others replied: "The Eastern Hall weeping existed because the emperor did not visit in person.

sentences.zh: 今陛下躬親撫視，羣臣從駕，臣等參議，以為不宜復哭。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty in person comforts and views; the ministers follow the imperial carriage—we your subjects jointly consider that one should not weep again.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty will comfort the bier in person and the ministers will follow your carriage—we hold there should be no second weeping."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「若大司馬戚尊位重，必哭於東堂，而廣川既是諸王之子，又年位尚幼，卿等議之，朕無異焉。

translations.literal: An edict said: "If the Grand Marshal is kin of weighty rank and position, one must weep in the Eastern Hall; yet Guangchuan is both a prince's son and still young in years and rank—you may deliberate as you will; I have no objection.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "For the Grand Marshal, kin of the highest rank, the Eastern Hall is required; but Guangchuan is a prince's son and still young in years and station—deliberate as you see fit; I raise no objection."

sentences.zh: 」諧將大殮，高祖素服深衣哭之，入室，哀慟，撫尸而出。

translations.literal: When Xie was about to undergo the great encoffment, Gaozu in plain white garments and deep mourning robes wept for him, entered the chamber, was stricken with grief, comforted the corpse, and went out.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of Xie's great encoffment Gaozu came in plain white and deep mourning, wept, entered the chamber, was overcome, comforted the corpse, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，廣川王妃薨於代京，未審以新尊從於卑舊，為宜卑舊來就新尊。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized: the Princess of Guangchuan died in the capital of Dai; it is unclear whether the newly honored should follow the humbler old, or the humbler old should come to the newly honored.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office reported: the Princess of Guangchuan died in the Dai capital; it was unclear whether the newly honored dead should follow the humbler old, or the humbler old should be brought to the newly honored.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「遷洛之人，自茲厥後，悉可歸骸邙嶺，皆不得就塋恒代。

translations.literal: An edict said: "For those who moved to Luoyang, from this time onward all may return their bones to Mount Mang; none may bury at the old tombs in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "For families who moved to Luoyang, from now on all may rest their bones on Mount Mang; none may bury in the old Dai tombs.

sentences.zh: 其有夫先葬在北，婦今喪在南，婦人從夫，宜還代葬；

translations.literal: Where the husband was first buried in the north and the wife now dies in the south, the woman follows the husband and should be returned for burial in Dai;
translations.idiomatic: If the husband was buried first in the north and the wife dies in the south, the wife follows the husband and should return to Dai for burial;

sentences.zh: 若欲移父就母，亦得任之。

translations.literal: if one wishes to move the father's grave to join the mother, that too may be done at will.
translations.idiomatic: if one wishes to move the father's grave to the mother's side, that may also be done.

sentences.zh: 其有妻墳於恒代，夫死於洛，不得以尊就卑；

translations.literal: Where the wife's tomb is in Dai and the husband dies in Luo, one may not let rank draw the lofty to the humble;
translations.idiomatic: If the wife's tomb lies in Dai and the husband dies in Luoyang, rank may not draw the lofty down to the humble;

sentences.zh: 欲移母就父，宜亦從之；

translations.literal: if one wishes to move the mother to join the father, that should also be followed;
translations.idiomatic: if one wishes to move the mother to the father, that should be allowed;

sentences.zh: 若異葬亦從之。

translations.literal: if separate burial is desired, that too may be followed.
translations.idiomatic: separate burial may also be chosen.

sentences.zh: 若不在葬限，身在代喪，葬之彼此，皆得任之。

translations.literal: If outside the burial limits, while the body lies in mourning in Dai, burial on either side may be done at will.
translations.idiomatic: If the case falls outside these limits and the mourner is in Dai, burial on either side is at choice.

sentences.zh: 其戶屬恒燕，身官京洛，去留之宜，亦從所擇。

translations.literal: Where household registers belong to Heng and Yan but office and person are in Jing and Luo, as to staying or leaving, that too follows choice.
translations.idiomatic: Where registers remain in Heng and Yan but office and person are in Jing and Luo, staying or leaving is likewise at choice.

sentences.zh: 其屬諸州者，各得任意。

translations.literal: Those attached to other provinces may each do as they wish.
translations.idiomatic: Those attached to other provinces may each decide for themselves."

sentences.zh: 」詔贈諧武衞將軍，諡曰剛。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made Xie General of Martial Guard; posthumous title Gang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made Xie General of Martial Guard and gave him the posthumous name Gang.

sentences.zh: 及葬，高祖親臨送之。

translations.literal: At the burial Gaozu in person attended and saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial Gaozu attended in person to see him off.

sentences.zh: 子靈道，襲。

translations.literal: His son Lingdao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lingdao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡悼王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Prince Dao.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Prince Dao.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 琛字曇寶，幼而敏慧，高祖愛之。

translations.literal: Chen, style Tanbao, was clever and quick as a child; Gaozu loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, styled Tanbao, was clever even as a child; Gaozu doted on him.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，拜定州刺史。

translations.literal: In Shizong's time he was appointed Inspector of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong he became Dingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 琛妃，世宗舅女，高皇后妹。

translations.literal: Chen's consort was Shizong's maternal niece, younger sister of Empress Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's consort was Shizong's niece by marriage, the younger sister of Empress Gao.

sentences.zh: 琛憑恃內外，多所受納，貪惏之極。

translations.literal: Chen relied on inside and outside connections and received many bribes; his greed knew no limit.
translations.idiomatic: Chen leaned on court and family ties and took endless bribes; his greed had no bottom.

sentences.zh: 及還朝，靈太后詔曰：「琛在定州，惟不將中山宮來，自餘無所不致，何可更復敍用。

translations.literal: When he returned to court, Empress Dowager Ling issued an edict: "At Dingzhou Chen failed only to carry off the Zhongshan Palace; otherwise there was nothing he would not seize—how can he be employed again?"
translations.idiomatic: On his return Empress Dowager Ling edicted: "In Dingzhou Chen took everything but the Zhongshan Palace itself—how can he be used again?"

sentences.zh: 」由是遂廢于家。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was dismissed and kept at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon dismissed and kept at home.

sentences.zh: 琛以肅宗始學，獻金字孝經。

translations.literal: When Suzong first began his studies, Chen presented a gilt-letter Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong first took up his studies, Chen presented a gilt-letter Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 又無方自達，乃與劉騰為養息，賂騰金寶巨萬計。

translations.literal: Having no other way to advance, he became Liu Teng's adopted son and bribed Teng with gold and jewels numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: With no other path forward he became Liu Teng's adopted son and paid him bribes in gold and jewels beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 騰屢為之言，乃得兼都官尚書，出為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Teng repeatedly spoke for him; he then obtained concurrent office as Director of the Court for the Imperial Clan and was sent out as Inspector of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Teng spoke for him again and again until he won the directorship of the Court for the Imperial Clan and went out as Qinzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 在州聚斂，百姓吁嗟。

translations.literal: In the province he amassed wealth; the common people groaned.
translations.idiomatic: In his province he amassed wealth while the people groaned.

sentences.zh: 屬東益、南秦二州氐反，詔琛為行臺，仍充都督，還攝州事。

translations.literal: When the Di of Eastern Yi and Southern Qin rebelled, an edict made Chen Mobile Office and still charged him as Commissioner, returning him to oversee the province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di of Eastern Yi and Southern Qin rebelled, an edict named him to a mobile office and kept him as commissioner while he resumed the provincial post.

sentences.zh: 琛性貪暴，既總軍省，求欲無厭，百姓患害，有甚狼虎。

translations.literal: Chen was by nature greedy and violent; holding both army and province he sought without end; the people suffered harm worse than from wolves and tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and brutal by nature, he now held army and province together and took without end; the people suffered worse than from wolves.

sentences.zh: 進討氐羌，大被摧破，士卒死者千數，率眾走還。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack the Di and Qiang, he suffered great defeat; a thousand soldiers died; he led the host in flight back.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against the Di and Qiang and was shattered; a thousand soldiers died and he fled with the remnant.

sentences.zh: 內恃劉騰，無所畏憚，為中尉糾彈，會赦，除名為民。

translations.literal: Relying within on Liu Teng, he feared nothing; the chief commandant impeached him; an amnesty came and he was stripped of name and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Backed by Liu Teng within, he feared nothing until the chief commandant impeached him; an amnesty spared his life but he was stripped of rank and made a commoner.

sentences.zh: 尋復王爵，後討鮮于脩禮，敗，免官爵。

translations.literal: Soon his princely title was restored; later in campaigning against Xianyu Xiuli he was defeated and stripped of office and title.
translations.idiomatic: His princely title was soon restored; later, campaigning against Xianyu Xiuli, he was defeated and lost office and title.

sentences.zh: 後討汾晉胡、蜀，卒於軍，追復王爵。

translations.literal: Later in campaigning against the Hu of Fen and Jin and the Shu, he died in the army; his princely title was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning against the Hu of Fen and Jin and the Shu, he died on campaign; his princely title was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 安豐王猛，字季烈。

translations.literal: Prince of Anfeng Meng, style Jilie.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, Prince of Anfeng, styled Jilie.

sentences.zh: 太和五年封，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed and made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 5 he received his fief and was made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 出為和龍鎮都大將、營州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Grand General of Helong Garrison and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as grand general of Helong garrison and Yingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 猛寬仁雄毅，甚有威略，戎夷畏愛之。

translations.literal: Meng was broad, benevolent, bold, and resolute, with great martial bearing; the frontier peoples feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng was broad, benevolent, bold, and resolute, with real martial presence; the frontier peoples both feared and loved him.

sentences.zh: 薨于州。

translations.literal: He died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his province.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，諡曰匡。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand Commandant; posthumous title Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant and given the posthumous name Kuang.

sentences.zh: 子延明，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yanming inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanming succeeded.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，授太中大夫。

translations.literal: In Shizong's time he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong he was made grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，歲大飢，延明乃減家財，以拯賓客數十人，并贍其家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanzhang, when the year brought great famine, Yanming then reduced his household wealth to save several dozen guests and also support their families.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yanzhang, in a year of great famine, Yanming spent his household wealth to save several dozen guests and support their families as well.

sentences.zh: 至肅宗初，為豫州刺史，甚有政績，累遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Suzong's reign he was made Inspector of Yu Province and had great administrative achievements; he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At Suzong's accession he became Yuzhou inspector with a strong record of governance and rose to attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 延明既博極羣書，兼有文藻，鳩集圖籍萬有餘卷。

translations.literal: Yanming had read exhaustively among the books and also possessed literary polish; he gathered more than ten thousand scrolls of maps and writings.
translations.idiomatic: Yanming had read widely and wrote well; he collected more than ten thousand scrolls of maps and books.

sentences.zh: 性清儉，不營產業。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure and frugal and did not pursue estates.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature frugal and did not amass property.

sentences.zh: 與中山王熙及弟臨淮王彧等，並以才學令望有名於世。

translations.literal: With the Prince of Zhongshan Xi and his younger brother the Prince of Linhuai Yu and others, all were famed in the world for talent, learning, and commanding esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He, Prince of Zhongshan Xi, and his younger brother Prince of Linhuai Yu were among those whose learning and reputation shone across the age.

sentences.zh: 雖風流造次不及熙、彧，而稽古淳篤過之。

translations.literal: Though in graceful ease and ready wit he did not match Xi and Yu, in investigating antiquity and plain earnestness he surpassed them.
translations.idiomatic: He lacked Xi and Yu's easy brilliance, but in scholarship and sober depth he outpaced them.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍中。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 詔與侍中崔光撰定服制。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him together with Palace Attendant Cui Guang to compile and fix ritual garb regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with Palace Attendant Cui Guang to draft court dress rules.

sentences.zh: 後兼尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Later he also held the concurrent post of Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He later served concurrently as right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 以延明博識多聞，敕監金石事。

translations.literal: Because Yanming was broadly learned and widely informed, he was commanded to oversee metal and stone inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: His wide learning earned him charge of epigraphic and bell-cauldron matters.

sentences.zh: 及元法僧反，詔為東道行臺、徐州大都督，節度諸軍事，與都督臨淮王彧、尚書李憲等討法僧。

translations.literal: When Yuan Faseng rebelled, an edict made him Eastern-Route Mobile Secretariat, Grand Commander of Xuzhou, and controller of all military affairs, to campaign against Faseng together with Commander-in-Chief the Prince of Linhuai Yu, Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Xian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Faseng rebelled, he was named eastern-route mobile secretariat and grand commander of Xuzhou, with command of all armies, and marched with Prince of Linhuai Yu, Minister Li Xian, and others against Faseng.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣其豫章王綜鎮徐州。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent his Prince of Yuzhang Zong to garrison Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan posted his Prince of Yuzhang, Zong, to hold Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 延明先牧徐方，甚得民譽，招懷舊土，遠近歸之。

translations.literal: Yanming had earlier governed the Xu region and won great praise among the people; he now rallied the old domain, and near and far submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Having once governed Xu with a strong popular name, he called back the old land and won submission from far and near.

sentences.zh: 綜既降，延明因以軍乘之，復東南之境，至宿豫而還。

translations.literal: Once Zong had surrendered, Yanming thereupon drove the army in pursuit, recovered the southeastern territory, and returned on reaching Suyu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong surrendered, Yanming pressed the pursuit, recovered the southeast as far as Suyu, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷都督、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander-in-chief and inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 頻經師旅，人物凋弊，延明招攜新故，人悉安業，百姓咸附。

translations.literal: The region had repeatedly suffered armies; people and goods were wasted and ruined; Yanming rallied new settlers and old residents alike, so that all settled into their trades and the common folk all attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: War had repeatedly ravaged the region; he gathered old and new inhabitants until every household had its livelihood and the people clung to him.

sentences.zh: 莊帝時，兼尚書令、大司馬。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Zhuang he concurrently held Minister of the Masters of Writing and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhuang he served concurrently as director of the Masters of Writing and grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 及元顥入洛，延明受顥委寄，率眾守河橋。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yanming received Hao's trust, led troops, and held Heqiao Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang, Yanming was entrusted with his cause and held Heqiao with an army.

sentences.zh: 顥敗，遂將妻子奔蕭衍，死於江南。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, he took wife and children and fled to Xiao Yan, and died in the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's fall sent him south to Xiao Yan with his family; he died in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 莊帝末，喪還。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Zhuang's reign his remains were returned.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhuangdi's reign his coffin came home.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，贈太保，王如故，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was posthumously given Grand Mentor, his princedom unchanged, posthumous title Wenzuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne he was posthumously titled grand mentor, his princedom left as before, with the temple name Prince Wenzuan.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦讚頌銘誄三百餘篇，又撰五經宗略、詩禮別義，注帝王世紀及列仙傳。

translations.literal: Works he authored—poems, fu, encomia, hymns, inscriptions, and dirges—numbered more than three hundred pieces; he also compiled Summaries of the Five Classics' Main Points and Separate Meanings of the Odes and Rites, and annotated Huangfu Mi's Chronological Record of Emperors and Kings and the Biographies of Transcendents.
translations.idiomatic: He left more than three hundred poems, fu, hymns, inscriptions, and dirges, compiled Summaries of the Five Classics and Separate Meanings of the Odes and Rites, and annotated the Chronological Record of Emperors and Kings and the Biographies of Transcendents.

sentences.zh: 又以河間人信都芳工算術，引之在館。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Xin Du Fang of Hejian was skilled in calculation and astronomy, he brought him into his household academy.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned Xin Du Fang of Hejian, a master of mathematics, to his library.

sentences.zh: 其撰古今樂事九章十二圖，又集器準九篇，芳別為之注，皆行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled nine chapters and twelve diagrams on music old and new, and also gathered nine chapters on instrument standards; Fang separately annotated them, and all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His nine chapters and twelve diagrams on music through the ages, and nine chapters on instrument measures with Fang's separate commentary, all circulated.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷二十 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」字，卷後當有宋人校語，傳本脫去。

translations.literal: In the table of contents of all editions of Wei shu juan 20 this scroll is marked "lacuna"; after the scroll there should have been Song-dynasty collation notes, lost in transmitted copies.
translations.idiomatic: Every Wei shu juan 20 table of contents marks this scroll "lacuna"; Song collation notes after the scroll are missing from transmitted copies.

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云：「魏收書闕，後人所補。

translations.literal: The Palace Edition textual verification states: "Wei Shou's book is lacunose here; later men supplemented it.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Edition notes: "Wei Shou's text is missing; later hands supplied this.

sentences.zh: 」檢傳文除少數字句外與北史卷一九文成五王傳同。

translations.literal: " On examination the transmitted text, apart from a few words and phrases, matches Beishi juan 19, Biographies of Wenzong's Five Princes.
translations.idiomatic: " The received text, save a few phrases, matches Beishi juan 19 (Wenzong's Five Princes).

sentences.zh: 孝元皇后生獻文皇帝 卷一三后妃傳文成元皇后單諡「元」，卷八三上外戚李峻傳

translations.literal: "Empress Xiaoyuan bore Emperor Xianwen": juan 13, Empresses and Consorts, has only "Empress Yuan" as posthumous title for Wenzong's Empress Yuan; juan 83 upper, Biography of Li Jun of the maternal kin,
translations.idiomatic: "Empress Xiaoyuan bore Emperor Xianwen": in juan 13 she is posthumous "Empress Yuan" only; juan 83 upper, Li Jun of the maternal kin,

translations.literal: 〈supplement〉
translations.idiomatic: supplement

sentences.zh: 、卷八九酷吏李洪之傳補也只稱「元皇后」，唯墓誌集釋元顥妃李元姜墓誌

translations.literal: and the supplement to juan 89, Biography of Li Hongzhi the Cruel Official, also speak only of "Empress Yuan"; only Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Hao's consort Lady Li Yuanchiang,
translations.idiomatic: and the juan 89 supplement on the cruel official Li Hongzhi likewise say only "Empress Yuan"; only Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Hao's consort Lady Li Yuanchiang,

sentences.zh: 〈圖版一八三〉

translations.literal: 〈plate 183〉
translations.idiomatic: plate 183

sentences.zh: 稱「元恭皇后」，但未見有「孝元」之號，疑「孝」乃「李」字之訛。

translations.literal: calls her "Empress Yuangong," but the style "Xiaoyuan" is nowhere seen; "Xiao" is suspected to be a corruption of "Li."
translations.idiomatic: titles her "Empress Yuangong," yet no "Xiaoyuan" title appears; "Xiao" likely corrupts "Li."

sentences.zh: 詮與李平高殖等四面攻燒 張森楷北史校勘記云：「高肇傳

translations.literal: "Quan with Li Ping, Gao Zhi, and others attacked and burned from four sides": Zhang Senkai's Beishi collation notes state: "Biography of Gao Zhao"
translations.idiomatic: "Quan, Li Ping, Gao Zhi, and others attacked and burned from four sides": Zhang Senkai's Beishi collation reads "Biography of Gao Zhao"

sentences.zh: 〈魏書卷八三下，即以北史卷八０補〉

translations.literal: 〈Wei shu juan 83 lower, supplied from Beishi juan 80〉
translations.idiomatic: Wei shu juan 83 lower (supplied from Beishi juan 80)

translations.literal: has "Zhi" with the plant graph for "Zhi" with the multiply graph.
translations.idiomatic: The text reads the plant-graph Zhi where the multiply-graph Zhi is meant.

sentences.zh: 按傳稱高植以濟州刺史「率州軍討破元愉，別將有功」，顯與此「高殖」為一人。

translations.literal: Commentary: The biography calls Gao Zhi, as inspector of Jizhou, "led provincial troops to defeat Yuan Yu, with separate-command merit," clearly the same man as this "Gao Zhi" with the multiply graph.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Gao Zhi as Jizhou inspector "led provincial troops to defeat Yuan Yu with merit as detached commander"—clearly this Gao Zhi with the multiply graph.

sentences.zh: 當時習慣人名地名常通用同音字，但這裏當是「植」字形訛。

translations.literal: At the time it was customary for personal and place names often to interchange homophonic characters, but here it should be a graphic corruption of "Zhi" with the plant graph.
translations.idiomatic: Homophones in names were common then, but here the plant-graph Zhi is clearly wrong.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎高聰等議曰 諸本「聰」作「敏」。

translations.literal: "Gao Cong and others of the Secretariat discussed and said": in various editions "Cong" is written "Min."
translations.idiomatic: "Secretariat attendant Gao Cong and others submitted": editions read Cong as Min (clever graph).

sentences.zh: 北史卷一九文成五王傳、冊府卷五八０

translations.literal: Beishi juan 19, Biographies of Wenzong's Five Princes; Cefu juan 580
translations.idiomatic: Beishi juan 19 (Wenzong Five Princes); Cefu juan 580

sentences.zh: 〈六九五七頁〉

translations.literal: 〈folio 6957〉
translations.idiomatic: folio 6957

sentences.zh: 作「聰」。

translations.literal: read "Cong."
translations.idiomatic: have "Cong."

sentences.zh: 按卷六八高聰傳，他在太和中自中書博士為侍郎，當時別無「高敏」其人，「敏」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Commentary: juan 68, Biography of Gao Cong, states that in the Taihe era he rose from Secretariat academician to attendant; at the time there was no such person as "Gao Min"; "Min" is corrupt and is now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note: juan 68 (Gao Cong) has him promoted from secretariat doctor to attendant in Taihe; no "Gao Min" then existed—Min is corrupt and the text is emended.

sentences.zh: 子靈道襲卒諡悼王 墓誌集釋元煥墓誌

translations.literal: "His son Lingdao succeeded, died, posthumous title Prince Dao": Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Huan
translations.idiomatic: "Son Lingdao inherited, died, titled Prince Dao": Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Huan

sentences.zh: 〈圖版一六一之二〉

translations.literal: 〈plate 161, no. 2〉
translations.idiomatic: plate 161, no. 2

sentences.zh: 「靈道」作「靈遵」，這裏「道」字當是「遵」形近而訛。

translations.literal: has "Lingzun" for "Lingdao"; here the character "dao" should be a near-form corruption of "zun."
translations.idiomatic: reads Lingzun for Lingdao; dao here is a near-graph corruption of zun.

sentences.zh: 又「悼王」作「哀王」，諸墓誌諡號不但常與史異，而且誌與誌也有不同，未必定是傳誤。

translations.literal: Moreover "Prince Dao" is "Prince Ai"; posthumous titles on epitaphs not only often differ from histories but differ epitaph to epitaph—not necessarily a biography error.
translations.idiomatic: "Prince Dao" appears as "Prince Ai" on epitaphs; posthumous titles often diverge from histories and from stone to stone—not necessarily a biographical error.

sentences.zh: 子祐字伯授 墓誌集釋元祐墓誌「授」作「援」，疑「授」字訛。

translations.literal: "His son You, styled Bosou": Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan You has "shou" with the hand-over graph written "yuan" with the aid graph; "shou" is suspected corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: "Son You, courtesy name Bosou": Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan You reads shou as yuan; shou is likely corrupt.
